subject: Integrate gs-quant offline risk metrics
task: 1. Add gs-quant==2.2.6 (pinned) to requirements.txt and verify pip install succeeds in the daemon environment BEFORE Monday. It pulls numpy/pandas/scipy/statsmodels; a dependency conflict found at 21:58Z is a disaster, found now it is a footnote.

2. Build scripts/trading/gs_metrics.py: adapter from our candle arrays to pd.Series WITH A DISTINCT DatetimeIndex (passing raw numpy raises AttributeError ndarray has no attribute shift - verified), calling only the 19 verified-working functions, returning plain JSON.

3. FIRST USE - highest value: run correlation + beta across the live book (ETH 0.5 short, XRP 1.0 short, BTC 0.05 sell stop). R829 claimed these are one bet at 3x size using notional arithmetic. If correlation > 0.7 this confirms it with a measured number and Monday sizing should follow.
4. Second use: max_drawdown across desk/archive/ telemetry (86MB, never statistically analysed).
5. Third use: Sharpe / realised vol on the near-miss cohort once it resolves.
doNotDo: Do NOT attempt GS API integration - no credentials exist, the README requires institutional client id/secret we will never have. Any GsSession init is dead code.
Do NOT use sharpe_ratio() until we supply our own risk-free rate - it throws MqUninitialisedError (verified) and will take a cycle down.
Do NOT use volatility() or exponential_volatility() on hourly data - both throw MqValueError multiple data points on same date (verified).
Do NOT assume technicals.trend() classifies trend - it is SEASONAL DECOMPOSITION, unrelated to our Q-5 regime bug.
licence: Apache-2.0 - permissive, we may vendor and modify. Not a trap.
orgSurvey: 73 public repos surveyed via GitHub API. 72 are infrastructure (Prometheus/Grafana/Spark/Kafka forks, Java ORM, Legend data-modelling). gs-quant is the ONLY trading repo. There is no second opportunity.
honestFraming: This is MEASUREMENT, not alpha. Our desk has been sizing without knowing its own correlation. A metrics library makes our knowledge of the trades better, not the trades themselves.
